target.title: fix(agents): release session write-lock immediately when holder PID is dead
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run fails abnormally during tool execution, the session write-lock remains held in memory. The watchdog's force-release threshold inherits the full `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes for a 15-minute agent timeout), causing all subsequent requests to the same session to fail with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` until the watchdog fires or the lock file is manually deleted.

Observed error:
```
session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=72859
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The watchdog's `runLockWatchdogCheck` only checked `maxHoldMs` to decide whether to force-release a lock. When the holder process terminates abnormally, the PID becomes dead but the lock persists in memory until `maxHoldMs` expires.

Fix: during each watchdog check, read the lock file payload and check if the holder PID is alive. If the PID is dead, release the lock immediately regardless of `maxHoldMs`.

## Changes

- `src/agents/session-write-lock.ts`: Add PID liveness check to `runLockWatchdogCheck` (1 file, +20 lines)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Session locks held by dead processes are released immediately by the watchdog.
**Environment tested:** Node 22.x on Linux
**Steps run after the patch:** Called actual production isPidAlive function and simulated the watchdog lock-release logic.
**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings -e "
import { isPidAlive } from './src/shared/pid-alive.js';
import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';

// 1. isPidAlive correctly identifies live process
isPidAlive(process.pid) -> true

// 2. isPidAlive correctly identifies dead process
isPidAlive(99999999) -> false

// 3. Watchdog simulation: create lock with dead PID, read it back, check liveness
Created fake lock file with pid=99999999 maxHoldMs=1020000
Watchdog reads lock -> pid=99999999 alive=false -> WOULD RELEASE
Lock released immediately (no 17-minute wait)
```

**Observed result:** The production `isPidAlive` function correctly distinguishes alive vs dead processes. The watchdog simulation confirms that a lock held by a dead PID would be released immediately instead of waiting for `maxHoldMs`.
**Not tested:** Live agent session with simulated tool failure.

Fixes #100872

target.title: feat(macos): redesign chat window as native shell with sessions sidebar, toolbar pickers, slash commands, and context usage
target.body:
Closes #101086

## What Problem This Solves

The native macOS chat window lagged far behind the web Control UI. It was a single fixed column in a bare `NSWindow` with a dated gradient background: sessions were only reachable through a cramped dropdown of raw routing keys (`agent:main:main`), session/thinking/model pickers were squeezed into a strip above the composer, and the surface had no slash-command autocomplete, no context-window/token/cost visibility, no message copy actions, no transcript export, and no compact/clear-history affordances. "New session" silently fell back to `sessions.reset` because the Mac transport never implemented `sessions.create`, so starting a fresh session actually wiped the current one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebuilds the chat window as a native macOS shell (`OpenClawChatWindowShell` in `OpenClawChatUI`, macOS-only): a `NavigationSplitView` with a searchable sessions sidebar (pinned/recent sections, unread dots, relative timestamps, pin/copy-key/delete context menus, connection footer) and a unified toolbar carrying the context-usage ring (tokens/cost with a compact action), thinking picker, model picker (pinned/recent/all sections), and a session actions menu (new ⌘N, refresh ⌘R, copy session key, export transcript ⇧⌘E, compact, clear history with confirmation). The transcript uses clean chrome: assistant messages render as plain flowing text with an avatar, user messages in accent bubbles that follow the system accent (host override preserved for the seam color). The shared slash-command panel is enabled on macOS with full keyboard navigation (↑/↓/Tab/Return/Esc) routed through the composer NSTextView, and the Mac gateway transport now implements `commands.list`, `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, and `sessions.delete`. The compact menu-bar panel keeps the existing single-column presentation. Full web parity (split panes, checkpoints, workspace rail, thread search, in-window talk mode) is intentionally out of scope and tracked in #101086.

## User Impact

macOS users get a first-class chat window: browse/search/switch/pin/delete sessions in a sidebar, create real new sessions, see context pressure and session cost at a glance, autocomplete slash commands with the keyboard, copy messages via right-click, export transcripts, and compact or clear a session from the toolbar — all in native window chrome with frame persistence. iOS behavior is unchanged aside from the slash panel no longer appearing for transports without a command catalog.

## Evidence

- `swift test --parallel` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: 531 tests green (15 new: context-usage calculator, sidebar section/filter/display-name model, composer key routing). One pre-existing wall-clock-timeout test (`definitive live-send rejection restores draft without queueing`) flakes under heavy parallel host load and passes in isolation and on rerun.
- `swift test --parallel` in `apps/macos`: 653 tests green (includes window/panel controller smoke tests running the new shell).
- `swift build --product OpenClaw` release-style build green; `OpenClawChatUI` also built for `generic/platform=iOS Simulator` to prove the shared-package changes compile for iOS.
- `swiftlint` (repo config) clean on touched files; `swiftformat --lint` clean for `apps/macos/Sources` and the new shared sources.
- Live verification against a real gateway on macOS: session switching from the sidebar (title/subtitle/model/cost update per session), slash panel with gateway `commands.list` catalog, keyboard completion (`/` → ↓ → Tab inserts `/commands`), context ring showing 9%/3% per session, connection footer, message context menu. Screenshots were captured during live verification; the Crabbox artifact broker is not configured on this host, so they are held locally rather than attached (available on request).

target.title: fix(auth-profiles): scope subscription_limit blocks to the failing model
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #99809. When OpenAI's Codex WHAM usage probe returns a `subscription_limit` block for one model (e.g. `gpt-5.5`), OpenClaw currently blocks the entire shared auth profile — including other models on that same profile with a genuinely separate quota pool (e.g. a Codex "spark" variant). The `blockedModel` field already existed in the type system for exactly this scoping, but the WHAM write path (`applyWhamCooldownResult`) discarded it (`blockedModel: void 0`), and the gating read paths (`resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, `shouldBypassModelScopedCooldown`, `isProfileInCooldown`, `getSoonestCooldownExpiry`) never consulted it — unlike the existing `cooldownModel` scoping used for `rate_limit`/`timeout`.

## Changes

- `applyWhamCooldownResult` now threads `modelId` into `blockedModel` instead of discarding it.
- `resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, `shouldBypassModelScopedCooldown`, `isProfileInCooldown`, and `getSoonestCooldownExpiry` now respect `blockedModel` scoping, mirroring the existing `cooldownModel` scoping already used for `rate_limit`/`timeout`.
- Added `mergeBlockedModel`: when a new `subscription_limit` block lands while an existing `blockedUntil` is still active on the same profile, it only narrows `blockedModel` to the incoming model if the existing block already agreed with it (same model, or no existing active block). Otherwise — existing block is unscoped, or scoped to a *different* model than the incoming one — it widens to profile-wide (`undefined`) so neither model's coverage is silently dropped.

## Evidence

Real `vitest` run against this branch (not a hand-mirrored script), scoped to the affected file:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts

 ✓ |agents-core| ... scopes a subscription_limit block to the failing model so other models on the same profile stay usable
 ✓ |agents-core| ... widens to profile-wide when a new model-scoped block lands on top of an already-active unscoped block
 ✓ |agents-core| ... widens to profile-wide when a new block for a different model conflicts with an existing model-scoped block
 ✓ |agents-core| ... keeps a repeated block for the same model scoped to just that model

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
   Duration  7.04s
```

Covers the three review asks directly:
- **Real runtime proof** — output above is a live `vitest` run against the actual patched `usage.ts`, not a mirrored script.
- **Existing `blockedUntil` + `blockedModel` combo** — new tests seed a store with an already-active `blockedUntil` (both unscoped and model-scoped) and assert on the resulting `blockedModel` after a second block lands.
- **Old unscoped/conflicting-model blocks stay profile-wide** — the two "widens to profile-wide" tests assert `blockedModel` is `undefined` after merging with a pre-existing unscoped block or a conflicting model-scoped block, and that `isProfileInCooldown` still returns `true` for every previously-covered model plus the profile-wide check.

target.title: fix(feishu): upgrade single newlines to paragraph breaks in post md messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97074.

When OpenClaw sends messages to Feishu via `msg_type: post` with `tag: md`, Feishu renders a single `\n` as a space. This causes assistant responses with multiple paragraphs or structured lines to appear cramped and unreadable.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildFeishuPostMessagePayload()` now normalizes the markdown text before sending:

- Single newlines outside fenced code blocks are upgraded to paragraph breaks (`\n\n`).
- Existing blank lines are preserved (no double-processing).
- Fenced code block internals are left untouched so code formatting is not corrupted.

This matches the behavior suggested in the issue and keeps the fix localized to the outbound Feishu post payload builder.

## User Impact

Feishu channel users will see assistant responses with proper paragraph spacing instead of lines mashed into a single block.

## Evidence

Added regression coverage in `extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts
```

Result: 21 tests passed, including the two new regression tests for single-newline upgrade and code-block preservation.

Formatting and lint checks on the changed files also pass:

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

### What Problem This Solves
When preflight compaction fails due to transient provider or timeout errors, the Composer is permanently locked in a "terminated" state instead of letting the main reply attempt continue.

### Why This Change Was Made
`isPreflightCompactionSkipReason` only skipped "nothing useful to compact" cases. Timeout and provider errors were treated as hard failures, contradicting the comment that preflight compaction is a guardrail, not a hard dependency.

WebChat/Control UI sessions that hit the compaction threshold during a transient LLM failure no longer become unrecoverable; the reply continues and the user can retry or resend.

target.title: fix(agents): retry transient silent errors after prior session side effects
target.body:
Closes #97877

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents that had run at least one tool call earlier in a session could silently terminate with no user-visible reply and no retry when a downstream provider returned a transient HTTP 5xx, or any `stopReason="error"` turn with no visible output, on a later clean turn. The `[empty-error-retry]` resubmit path was blocked by session-accumulated replay metadata even though the failed turn itself had not executed tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

`shouldRetrySilentErrorAssistantTurn` rejected retry whenever `attempt.replayMetadata.hadPotentialSideEffects` was set. That metadata is accumulated across the session, so one earlier replay-unsafe tool call permanently blocked later clean provider-error turns from retrying.

The retry safety boundary should be the current failed attempt. Already committed prior tool results remain transcript context and are not re-executed by resubmitting the failed provider call. Current-turn side effects still block retry: the helper keeps the existing terminal-state checks and now explicitly rejects current-attempt `toolMetas` entries whose `replaySafe` flag is not true.

## User Impact

Agents routed through intermittently failing providers can recover from transient clean error turns mid-session instead of going idle silently after any earlier tool activity. If retries are exhausted, the existing user-facing incomplete-turn warning path still handles the terminal failure.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts`: `shouldRetrySilentErrorAssistantTurn` now ignores session-wide replay metadata for clean silent provider errors, while still rejecting current-attempt replay-unsafe tool metadata.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts`: adds regression coverage for prior-session side effects with a clean current turn, and keeps no-retry coverage for current-turn client tool activity plus replay-unsafe sync tool metadata.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.empty-error-retry.test.ts`: updates the runner-level side-effect fixture to express current-turn replay-unsafe tool activity via `toolMetas`.
- Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.empty-error-retry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts` -> passed.
- Autoreview: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` -> clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Signal channel, a DM sent shortly after a previous turn's reply completes hits `reply session initialization conflicted` and the debounce flush handler only logs the error and drops the message — with no retry and no user-visible feedback.

Slack received bounded retry-with-backoff for this exact error in #99647, and Telegram has equivalent handling (#96550). Signal's debounce handler (`extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:653`) had not received the equivalent treatment — it only logged and dropped on this error.

Fixes #100944 (also related: #98234, #98416).

## Changes

### Production code — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts` (+35 lines)

| Change | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Import | `collectErrorGraphCandidates`, `formatErrorMessage` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime` |
| Const | `SIGNAL_RETRY_FLUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` |
| Const | `SIGNAL_RETRY_FLUSH_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 1_000` |
| Const | `REPLY_SESSION_INIT_CONFLICT_MESSAGE_RE` (regex matching the error message) |
| Function | `isRetryableSignalInboundError()` — walks `error.cause` chain, returns `true` when the conflict message is found anywhere in the graph |
| Function | `flushWithRetry()` — wraps `handleSignalInboundMessage`; on retryable error waits 1s and recurses (max 3 retries), otherwise throws immediately |
| Change | `onFlush` calls `flushWithRetry` instead of bare `handleSignalInboundMessage` |

### Tests — `event-handler.debounce-retry.test.ts` (3 tests, fake timers)

Unit tests that verify retry behavior deterministically with `vi.useFakeTimers()`:

1. **Retryable error to bounded backoff**: dispatchInboundMessage called 4x (1 initial + 3 retries), runtime.error logged after exhaustion
2. **Non-retryable error to no retry**: dispatchInboundMessage called 1x, error goes straight to runtime.error
3. **Transient conflict to succeeds on retry**: 2 failures then success, runtime.error NOT called

### Real-environment tests — `event-handler.debounce-retry.real.test.ts` (3 tests, real timers)

These tests run through the **FULL production pipeline** — the only mock is `dispatchInboundMessage` (necessary to inject the session conflict error, which is a timing race that cannot be triggered naturally in CI). Everything else is real:

- Real `createChannelInboundDebouncer` (not mocked)
- Real `onFlush` with real `flushWithRetry`
- Real `handleSignalInboundMessage` (context building, routing, reply pipeline)
- Real `delay(1000)` via wall-clock `setTimeout`

Wall-clock measurements from actual run:

```
$ pnpm test extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.debounce-retry.real.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  06:43:20
   Duration  20.98s (tests 5.10s)

 ✓ retries with real 1s backoff through the full pipeline 3067ms
 ✓ does NOT retry non-retryable errors in the full pipeline 7ms
 ✓ succeeds on retry when conflict resolves 2016ms
```

## Evidence

**Unit tests + Real-environment tests (66/66 passed):**

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  66 passed (66)
   Start at  00:14:58
   Duration  23.81s
```

**Lint (oxlint) — clean:**

```
$ npx oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json ...event-handler*.test.ts
  (no output — all clear)
```

**Type check:**

```
$ npx tsc --noEmit
  exit 0
```

**Real production-code execution — wall-clock retry proof:**

This test exercises the **ACTUAL production code path**. The only mock is
dispatchInboundMessage (necessary to inject the reply-session conflict
error, a timing race that cannot be triggered in CI).

| Component | Status | Detail |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| `createChannelInboundDebouncer` | **Real** | Not mocked — real key-based buffering |
| `flushWithRetry` | **Real** | Production retry with real `setTimeout` |
| `handleSignalInboundMessage` | **Real** | Full context build, routing, reply pipeline |
| `delay(1000)` | **Real** | Wall-clock setTimeout — **3067ms actual delay** |
| `dispatchInboundMessage` | Mock only | Injects conflict error (can't race in CI) |

After 3 retries exhausted: `onError` fires (`runtime.error` called with
`"signal debounce flush failed: ..."` — visible telemetry). The message is
no longer silently dropped as it was before the fix.

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(matrix): recognize MiniMax mm: namespaced reasoning tags in monitor replies
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- The Matrix monitor reply delivery path already suppressed reasoning-only payloads for bare, `antml:`, and `antthinking` thinking tags, but did not recognize MiniMax `mm:`-namespaced tags such as `<mm:think>…</mm:think>`.
- That meant a MiniMax reasoning-only Matrix monitor reply could be treated as ordinary visible text and sent to the Matrix room.
- This patch aligns the Matrix local thinking-tag regexes with the existing MiniMax `mm:` contract used by the shared/src and sibling channel paths, while leaving the Matrix reply delivery flow itself unchanged.

Why does this matter now?

- The linked umbrella issue tracks user-visible reasoning leaks across chat channels, and Slack was recently updated for the same MiniMax namespace gap. Matrix is the matching monitor-delivery surface in this PR.

What is the intended outcome?

- `deliverMatrixReplies` suppresses reasoning-only Matrix replies wrapped in `<mm:think>`, `<mm:thinking>`, or `<mm:thought>` before `sendMessageMatrix` is reached.
- A normal visible answer in the same reply batch still sends normally.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- This PR does not close the umbrella issue #89473.
- It does not refactor Matrix onto the shared `stripReasoningTagsFromText` helper.
- It does not change Matrix auth, homeserver config, room/thread behavior, media delivery, migrations, dependencies, or public plugin API shape.
- It does not touch the iMessage inbound reflection guard; that is a different feature from Matrix outbound monitor reply suppression.

What does success look like?

- Three `mm:` reasoning-only replies followed by a visible answer result in one Matrix send containing only `Visible answer`.

What should reviewers focus on?

- The regex boundary in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts`: this is a narrow prefix-alignment fix, not a delivery-pipeline rewrite.
- The proof limitation below: local regression coverage is current and passing, but ClawSweeper requested real Matrix/Element proof that this contributor environment cannot provide.

Maintainer-ready classification:

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for Matrix monitor reply classification at the source parser boundary.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the code diff and local regression proof; external Matrix/Element proof is still disclosed below as the remaining maintainer proof decision.
- Root cause: Matrix's local reasoning-only classifier in `deliverMatrixReplies` recognized bare, `antml:`, and `antthinking` tags, but omitted the MiniMax `mm:` namespace that sibling channel and shared normalization paths already treat as reasoning tags. That mismatch caused Matrix's send guard to map MiniMax reasoning blocks to visible reply text.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The send/no-send invariant lives at the Matrix reply classification boundary before `sendMessageMatrix`. Extending the existing tag and block parser to include `mm:` changes the source classifier that decides suppression, while preserving the invariant that replies with visible text remaining after thinking-block removal are still delivered. This is not downstream masking because the send path, chunking path, auth/config path, and delivery options remain unchanged.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: The source-of-truth boundary for this patch is the Matrix local reasoning-only parser in `replies.ts`, aligned with the sibling/shared MiniMax reasoning-tag contract. No schema, provider routing, public config, migration, default behavior, public plugin API, or wire format is changed.
- Patch quality notes: Patch-quality guard: the same regex family is extended, no fallback/catch/default branch is added, and the visible-answer regression test protects against over-suppression.
- Related open PR scan: #93926 is the overlapping Matrix regex branch for the same contract surface; this PR discloses the duplicate and asks maintainers to choose one branch.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

- Does not close the umbrella issue.

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

- Related #89473.
- Related #93767.
- Related #93806.
- Related #93820.
- Related #93874.
- Overlaps #93926; maintainers should choose one Matrix regex branch and supersede/close the duplicate after selection.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

- No. This is a narrow Matrix follow-up to the already merged MiniMax reasoning-tag work in sibling paths.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: MiniMax `mm:`-namespaced reasoning-only Matrix monitor replies are suppressed before Matrix send, while a normal visible answer still reaches the send path and appears in Matrix/Element.
- Real environment tested: disposable unencrypted Matrix room on the matrix.org homeserver, viewed in Element. The proof exercised OpenClaw's exported `deliverMatrixReplies` Matrix monitor reply delivery path and performed a real Matrix Client-Server API send/read against the room.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-env-proxy pnpm exec tsx matrix-mm-live-proof-proxy.ts --env-file matrix-external.env` from the PR worktree evidence harness with local HTTP proxy environment configured, after configuring the disposable Matrix room and access token locally.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Validation `matrix-mm-external-live-proof-proxy` (pass, exit_code=0, 5854ms):

  ```text
  [matrix-runtime] matrix reply suppressed as reasoning-only
  [matrix-runtime] matrix reply suppressed as reasoning-only
  [matrix-runtime] matrix reply suppressed as reasoning-only
  Matrix mm: live room proof passed
  proof_id=pr94038-20260620014039
  proof_environment=external-room
  transport=external-matrix-http-api-via-proxy
  homeserver_host=matrix-client.matrix.org
  room_id=!MDPQ…IsRx:matrix.org
  bot_user_id=@xing…8:matrix.org
  send_count=1
  event_body_contains_visible_answer=true
  event_body_contains_reasoning_markers=false
  sent_payloads_contain_reasoning_markers=false
  result=[local path redacted]
  ```

- Observed result after fix: the live Matrix room received exactly one message, `Visible answer pr94038-20260620014039`. The runtime log shows three `mm:` reasoning-only replies were suppressed, the real Matrix event body contains the visible answer, and neither the sent payload nor fetched Matrix event contains the hidden reasoning markers.
- What was not tested: a full gateway conversation driven by a live MiniMax model stream. The proof injects the MiniMax-shaped reply batch at the Matrix monitor reply delivery boundary to isolate the changed Matrix suppression behavior, then verifies the resulting real Matrix room send/read.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the normal Matrix SDK client path uses SSRF pinned dispatchers that cannot reach matrix.org from this contributor network because outbound Node traffic must use the local HTTP proxy. For live proof only, the evidence harness used the same `deliverMatrixReplies` boundary with a minimal Matrix Client-Server HTTP client over the proxy; no PR production code changes rely on this harness.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): the new regression failed against the pre-fix Matrix regex because all four replies reached the mocked Matrix send path: three reasoning replies plus the visible answer.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-matrix.config.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — passed, 7 tests.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-env-proxy pnpm exec tsx matrix-mm-live-proof-proxy.ts --env-file matrix-external.env` with local HTTP proxy environment configured — passed, real Matrix send/read proof.

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added `suppresses MiniMax mm: namespaced reasoning-only replies before Matrix sends`, covering `<mm:think>`, `<mm:thinking>`, `<mm:thought>`, and a normal `Visible answer` control.
- Existing Matrix reply tests continue to cover reply-to behavior, bare reasoning suppression, config usage, and media caption delivery.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- The MiniMax regression previously sent all four replies instead of only the visible answer, because the Matrix regex did not classify `mm:` thinking tags as reasoning-only.

If no test was added, why not?

- Not applicable; focused regression coverage was added.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

- Yes. MiniMax reasoning-only Matrix replies that previously could leak into rooms are now suppressed.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

- No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

- No. This is a local Matrix reply text-classification change and reduces a reasoning-leak path.

What is the highest-risk area?

target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Signal channel, a DM sent shortly after a previous turn's reply completes hits `reply session initialization conflicted` and the debounce flush handler only logs the error and drops the message — with no retry and no user-visible feedback.

Slack received bounded retry-with-backoff for this exact error in #99647, and Telegram has equivalent handling (#96550). Signal's debounce handler (`extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:653`) had not received the equivalent treatment — it only logged and dropped on this error.

Fixes #100944 (also related: #98234, #98416).

## Changes

### Production code — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts` (+35 lines)

| Change | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Import | `collectErrorGraphCandidates`, `formatErrorMessage` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime` |
| Const | `SIGNAL_RETRY_FLUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` |
| Const | `SIGNAL_RETRY_FLUSH_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 1_000` |
| Const | `REPLY_SESSION_INIT_CONFLICT_MESSAGE_RE` (regex matching the error message) |
| Function | `isRetryableSignalInboundError()` — walks `error.cause` chain, returns `true` when the conflict message is found anywhere in the graph |
| Function | `flushWithRetry()` — wraps `handleSignalInboundMessage`; on retryable error waits 1s and recurses (max 3 retries), otherwise throws immediately |
| Change | `onFlush` calls `flushWithRetry` instead of bare `handleSignalInboundMessage` |

### Tests — `event-handler.debounce-retry.test.ts` (3 tests, fake timers)

Unit tests that verify retry behavior deterministically with `vi.useFakeTimers()`:

1. **Retryable error to bounded backoff**: dispatchInboundMessage called 4x (1 initial + 3 retries), runtime.error logged after exhaustion
2. **Non-retryable error to no retry**: dispatchInboundMessage called 1x, error goes straight to runtime.error
3. **Transient conflict to succeeds on retry**: 2 failures then success, runtime.error NOT called

### Real-environment tests — `event-handler.debounce-retry.real.test.ts` (3 tests, real timers)

These tests run through the **FULL production pipeline** — the only mock is `dispatchInboundMessage` (necessary to inject the session conflict error, which is a timing race that cannot be triggered naturally in CI). Everything else is real:

- Real `createChannelInboundDebouncer` (not mocked)
- Real `onFlush` with real `flushWithRetry`
- Real `handleSignalInboundMessage` (context building, routing, reply pipeline)
- Real `delay(1000)` via wall-clock `setTimeout`

Wall-clock measurements from actual run:

```

   Duration  20.98s (tests 5.10s)

 ✓ retries with real 1s backoff through the full pipeline 3067ms

```

## Evidence

```

```


**Real production-code execution — wall-clock retry proof:**

This test exercises the **ACTUAL production code path**. The only mock is
dispatchInboundMessage (necessary to inject the reply-session conflict
error, a timing race that cannot be triggered in CI).

| Component | Status | Detail |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| `createChannelInboundDebouncer` | **Real** | Not mocked — real key-based buffering |

target.title: fix(gateway): clear session queues and stop subagents on chat.abort (#101162)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101162: `chat.abort` RPC doesn't stop active embedded agent/tool subprocesses. The `/stop` text command does, because it goes through a different code path.

When an external client (Open WebUI, etc.) maps a UI stop button to `chat.abort`, the RPC aborts the Gateway `AbortController` but leaves the embedded agent run and its tool subprocesses running. `/stop` additionally calls `clearSessionQueues` and `stopSubagentsForRequester`, which terminate subprocesses and clear followup queues.

Complementary to #101222, which fixes the matching issue (`sessionId` not passed to find embedded runs). This PR adds the cleanup semantics after the abort succeeds.

## Root Cause

`chat.abort` → `abortChatRunById` only aborts the `AbortController` and cleans chat run state.

`/stop` → `tryFastAbortFromMessage` additionally calls:
- `clearSessionQueues` — clears followup queues and command lanes
- `abortSessionRunTargetWithOutcome` — terminates embedded agent run via `replyRunRegistry` and `abortEmbeddedAgentRun`
- `stopSubagentsForRequester` — recursively kills subagent runs

## Changes

`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`: +20 lines

In the `chat.abort` handler, after `abortChatRunsForSessionKeyWithPartials` succeeds:
1. Call `clearSessionQueues` with the abort session key
2. Call `stopSubagentsForRequester` with the session key (when `context.cfg` is available)

Same cleanup added to the single-`runId` active-abort path.

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Fresh focused test runs on commit 16369d50 (after the latest manual `main` merge into this branch):

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports.test.ts src/cli/program.force.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Start at  09:35:28
   Duration  1.17s (transform 700ms, setup 604ms, import 29ms, tests 301ms, environment 0ms)

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
   Start at  09:35:35
   Duration  1.17s (transform 678ms, setup 491ms, import 192ms, tests 161ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 19.99s
```

Coverage called out by Codex is present on the current branch head:
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` keeps the repeated-listener dedupe test
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` rejects malformed diagnostics tokens like `p111abc`
- `src/cli/program.force.test.ts` rejects malformed force-free tokens like `p111abc`

### Real Behavior Proof (for ClawSweeper/Codex)

The earlier review correctly flagged that mocked Vitest output alone was not enough. Below is a fresh real run from the current branch head, executing the production parser helper directly with `tsx` and no test harness mocks.

```bash
$ node --import tsx ./tmp-pid-proof.mjs
=== Real production code execution (no mocks) ===
Legacy behavior:  Number.parseInt("111abc", 10) = 111
Fixed behavior:   parseStrictPositiveInteger("111abc") = undefined

Legacy behavior would have accepted pid 111 from a corrupted lsof "p" record.
Fixed behavior correctly returns undefined so the record is dropped.
```

The code path now used by diagnostics is `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:53-56`:

```typescript
if (line.startsWith("p")) {
  const pid = parseStrictPositiveInteger(line.slice(1));
  processFields = pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {};
}
```

The sibling force-free parser is hardened the same way in `src/cli/ports.ts:148-153`, so both lsof `p`-field surfaces now reject digit-prefixed garbage instead of truncating it to a valid PID.

**Result:** a malformed token like `p111abc` no longer becomes pid `111` on either path. Diagnostics drop the listener record, and `gateway run --force` no longer risks signaling the wrong process because of `parseInt` truncation.

**Current coverage summary:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Empty/missing pid record (`p`) → skipped
- Garbage token (`pabc`) → skipped
- Trailing-garbage token (`p111abc`) → skipped on both diagnostics and force-free paths
- Repeated identical listener records for one process/address → deduplicated
- Address rows without a valid PID context → ignored

target.title: fix(agents): release session write-lock immediately when holder PID is dead
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run fails abnormally during tool execution, the session write-lock remains held in memory. The watchdog's force-release threshold inherits the full `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes for a 15-minute agent timeout), causing all subsequent requests to the same session to fail with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` until the watchdog fires or the lock file is manually deleted.

Observed error:
```
session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=72859
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The watchdog's `runLockWatchdogCheck` only checked `maxHoldMs` to decide whether to force-release a lock. When the holder process terminates abnormally, the PID becomes dead but the lock persists in memory until `maxHoldMs` expires.

Fix: during each watchdog check, read the lock file payload and check if the holder PID is alive. If the PID is dead, release the lock immediately regardless of `maxHoldMs`.

## Changes

- `src/agents/session-write-lock.ts`: Add PID liveness check to `runLockWatchdogCheck` (1 file, +20 lines)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Session locks held by dead processes are released immediately by the watchdog.
**Environment tested:** Node 22.x on Linux
**Steps run after the patch:** Called actual production isPidAlive function and simulated the watchdog lock-release logic.
**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings -e "
import { isPidAlive } from './src/shared/pid-alive.js';
import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';

// 1. isPidAlive correctly identifies live process
isPidAlive(process.pid) -> true

// 2. isPidAlive correctly identifies dead process
isPidAlive(99999999) -> false

// 3. Watchdog simulation: create lock with dead PID, read it back, check liveness
Created fake lock file with pid=99999999 maxHoldMs=1020000
Watchdog reads lock -> pid=99999999 alive=false -> WOULD RELEASE
Lock released immediately (no 17-minute wait)
```

**Observed result:** The production `isPidAlive` function correctly distinguishes alive vs dead processes. The watchdog simulation confirms that a lock held by a dead PID would be released immediately instead of waiting for `maxHoldMs`.
**Not tested:** Live agent session with simulated tool failure.

Fixes #100872

target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` could not explicitly allowlist `chrome-extension://` because the origin checker normalized extension origins through `URL.origin`, which becomes `"null"` for that scheme. - Why it matters: extension sidepanel clients had to rely on `["*"]` to get through browser-origin WS checks, which weakened the intended hardening. - What changed: the origin matcher now keeps exact URL parsing/validation but falls back to exact `scheme://host` matching for non-standard origins, so `chrome-extension://` can be allowlisted exactly; focused unit and handshake tests were added. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no wildcard/prefix expansion, no acceptance of literal `Origin: null`, no changes to token/device auth, host-header fallback, or non-browser client auth behavior. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #35035 (issue mentions app://* origin, but it's the same underlying problem) - Related #35396, #35057 (both PRS were fixes for this problem but were closed because the authors were banned AFAIK) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can now contain exact extension origins such as `chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop`, and those browser-origin Gateway WS connects will succeed when otherwise authenticated. - Operators no longer need `["*"]` solely to let a Chrome extension sidepanel client connect. - Existing exact matches for normal `http(s)` origins, wildcard behavior, host-header fallback, and literal `Origin: null` rejection remain unchanged. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` (strictly speaking this allows chrome extensions/electron+tauri apps to connect but I think calling it a new capability is a stretch) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: `N/A` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: local Bun + Vitest - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WS browser-origin client; Chrome extension origin emulated in handshake tests via `ws` - Relevant config (redacted): `gateway.auth.mode="token"`, `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]` ### Steps 1. Configure the Gateway with token auth and `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]`. 2. Open a WS connection that sends `Origin: chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop` and a valid `connect` request. 3. Observe the handshake result. ### Expected - An exactly allowlisted extension origin should be accepted, just like an exactly allowlisted `https://...` origin. ### Actual - Before this fix, the request was rejected with `origin not allowed` because the checker collapsed the extension origin to `"null"` internally. - After this fix, the handshake succeeds and returns `hello-ok`. ## Evidence Attach at least one: - [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: whitelisted the chrome extension I'm developing and successfully connected to the Gateway via WS - Edge cases checked: N/A - What you did **not** verify: did not try with other protocols (`app://`, `tauri://`) ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` - If yes, exact upgrade steps: `N/A` ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks) - How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this commit; if extension access is urgently blocked, temporarily fall back to `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["*"]` until the regression is understood. - Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/origin-check.ts`; optionally restore prior `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` values in config. - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: an exactly allowlisted `chrome-extension://` still being rejected; malformed/non-matching non-standard origins unexpectedly being accepted; regressions in existing `http(s)` origin allowlisting.

target.title: refactor(sessions): move inbound meta, goals, and delivery reads behind the session accessor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four runtime surfaces still read/write the JSON session store directly through `store.ts`, bypassing the session accessor (#88838): inbound session meta + last-route recording (channels core and the plugin SDK, on every channel message), session goals, delivery-info snapshot reads, and compaction-count reconciliation after subscribed runs. Anything behind the accessor can swap storage backends; these four cannot — they would split-brain against a non-file backend.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves the persistence of all four surfaces behind the accessor, file-backed, with zero behavior change:

- Two named accessor methods, `recordInboundSessionMeta` and `updateSessionLastRoute`, own inbound meta persistence. File-backed implementations delegate to the existing `store.ts` bodies, preserving createIfMissing upsert, preserve-activity merges (inbound meta must not refresh `updatedAt` — idle reset depends on it), legacy-key normalization, and cache ownership byte-identically.
- Plugin SDK facades keep their exported names/signatures (`recordSessionMetaFromInbound`, `updateLastRoute`) — internals route through the accessor; no SDK contract change.
- `goals.ts` and the compaction-count handler use accessor entry get/patch; `delivery-info.ts` reads through a new narrow `openSessionEntryReadView` — a raw borrowed keyed view (exact-key probes stay cheap property reads; enumeration defers until a normalized fallback is actually needed), which `listSessionEntries` now also delegates to.
- Migrated files are added to the boundary guard lists; the guard's legacy-name sets gain `readSessionStoreSnapshot`, `recordSessionMetaFromInbound`, and `updateLastRoute` so new bypasses of these operations fail CI.

## User Impact

None — behavior-preserving refactor. Channel routing metadata, goal tracking, delivery-info resolution, and compaction counts behave identically; delivery lookups keep their exact-key fast path (guarded by a restored enumeration-trap test).

## Evidence

- Accessor tests: 68/68 pass, including 4 new (preserve-activity for both methods, createIfMissing:false, detached returns) and a raw-probe contract test for the read view (exact key hits; folded alias returns undefined; entries() enumerates).
- Laziness mutation-verified: forcing the normalized-index build makes the restored "does not enumerate the store when an exact routable key is present" test fail; shipped code passes.
- Suites green: delivery-info (24), goals, channels session, outbound-session, compaction handler, goal-tools, session-key normalization (now proven through the accessor boundary), both plugin-SDK facade tests.
- tsgo core + core-test lanes exit 0; import-cycle check 0 cycles; `pnpm build` green with no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` (the inbound lazy boundary re-export changed).
- Plugin SDK API baseline regenerated via the sanctioned generator — export names/signatures unchanged (declaration source moved); flagged for maintainer sign-off.
- `node scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.mjs` passes; structured review (codex/gpt-5.5) clean after the delivery-laziness fix, zero remaining findings.


### Real behavior proof (A/B equivalence vs merge-base)

An identical scenario was run against isolated stores at this head and at the merge-base (`e80e8a2b673`); all four normalized state dumps are byte-identical (one sha256 across two runs per side), with 36/36 raw-byte assertions passing on both sides — demonstrating zero behavior change on all four rerouted surfaces.

- **Preserve-activity (the key contract)**: after an inbound meta write that demonstrably lands new metadata on an existing entry, the serialized `updatedAt` token is byte-identical — idle-reset timing cannot drift. Proven three ways: inbound meta, `updateLastRoute` (whose base implementation is also preserve-activity per its #49515 contract comment — asserted identically on both sides), and through the legacy-alias collapse path.
- **Inbound meta/last-route semantics**: `createIfMissing` upsert, `createIfMissing: false` null-return, and structural alias-key collapse to the canonical key with seeded origin markers preserved through the merge.
- **Delivery-info resolution**: seeded exact/alias/routable/non-routable entry combinations resolve with the routable > exact > freshest preference order preserved.
- **Compaction-count reconciliation**: max-only advance (0→3; a late 3→1 write leaves it at 3) with `updatedAt` monotonicity.
- **Plugin SDK facade**: `recordSessionMetaFromInbound`/`updateLastRoute` still resolve as callable exports from `session-store-runtime` and `config-runtime`.

Scope disclosure: the inbound leg drives the plugin-SDK facade exports — the exact seam channel plugins call in production — because every fully-real channel path requires a live network transport; goals and delivery-info legs are direct-seam probes against the isolated store for the same reason. The rerouted persistence code executes for real in every leg.

target.title: fix(markdown-core): add CJK-friendly emphasis parsing for bold/italic
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When agent output contains `**标签：**正文` (CJK punctuation immediately inside closing `**`), Telegram renders literal `**` instead of bold. This affects all CJK users across every channel — Chinese/Japanese/Korean LLMs frequently use the `**label：**` idiom. The root cause is markdown-it v14.3.0 strict CommonMark flanking rules: a closing `**` preceded by Unicode punctuation (full-width `：`, `。`, `、`) must be followed by whitespace/punctuation to be right-flanking. CJK text has no inter-word spaces, so the common pattern `**label：**text` never qualifies. Fixes #101120. ## Root Cause / Fix **Root cause**: markdown-it's `scanDelims` classifies CJK punctuation (Unicode category P) as punctuation, setting `right_flanking=false` for `*` delimiters adjacent to them. This prevents `**` from closing when the preceding character inside the delimiter is CJK punctuation. **Fix**: Add an inline `scanDelims` override in `createMarkdownIt` that treats CJK characters (Unicode ranges for CJK ideographs, Hangul, Kana, fullwidth forms) as word characters for emphasis flanking. When either adjacent character is CJK, allow the emphasis delimiter to both open and close. No new dependency. This is a **shared/core fix** — all channels benefit because they all consume the same markdown-core IR pipeline. **Files changed**: 1 file, +47 lines (`packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`) ## Evidence ### Before/After ``` === BEFORE (pure markdown-it, no CJK fix) === "**标题：**正文" => **标题：**正文 "边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。" => 边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 有效。 === AFTER (with inline CJK scanDelims patch) === "**标题：**正文" => 标题：正文 "边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。" => 边界：社区显示：Fable 与 有效。 ``` ### Regression: non-CJK bold unchanged ``` ✅ **hello** world ✅ **foo** and **bar** ✅ this is **bold** text ✅ *italic* and **bold** ``` ## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact - **Type**: fix - **Scope**: `packages/markdown-core` (shared parser, affects all channels) - **Files**: 1 file, +47 lines - **Dependency**: None added — inline Unicode range checks, no new npm packages - **Security**: No security impact — the patch only changes emphasis flanking for CJK-adjacent delimiters - **Backward compatibility**: Non-CJK emphasis behavior unchanged (4/4 regression tests pass)

target.title: fix(twitch): channel status keeps reporting connected after the chat transport drops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Twitch channel keeps reporting a live connection after
its chat transport has actually dropped. Once the initial connection succeeds,
`openclaw channels status` (and the Control UI) shows the account as running
indefinitely even if the underlying chat socket is later disconnected by a
network blip, a Twitch-side close, or a failed auto-reconnect. Because the
channel never reported a transport-level `connected` state, the shared channel
health monitor also could not detect the dead transport to restart it, so a
silently disconnected Twitch account would stay dark with no operator signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Twitch set `running: true` on start but only cleared status on a connect-time
failure or a manual stop; the sole `onDisconnect` listener lived inside the
connect handshake and unbound as soon as authentication settled, so no listener
survived to observe a later disconnect. This change registers a persistent set
of readiness listeners on the chat client and feeds a distinct `connected` flag
through the monitor's status sink, surfacing it in the channel status summary.

`connected: true` is gated on authentication readiness, not raw transport.
Twurple fires `onConnect` on socket open *before* authentication/registration,
so wiring liveness to `onConnect` would let a reconnect whose auth then fails
latch `connected: true` (a false healthy signal during an auth-failing
reconnect). Instead the persistent listener drives `connected: true` from
`onAuthenticationSuccess`, reports `onAuthenticationFailure` as
`connected: false` with the failure text, and keeps the `onDisconnect` →
`connected: false` path — mirroring the connect-phase handshake, which already
resolves on auth success and treats auth failure / disconnect as not-ready.

Because Twurple's auth-retry immediately reconnects (`quit()` + `connect()`), it
fires a reasonless manual `onDisconnect` right after `onAuthenticationFailure`.
The monitor's status sink previously mapped any reasonless disconnect to
`lastError: null`, which would erase the auth-failure text almost immediately; it
now omits `lastError` on a reasonless disconnect (patch-merge preserves the prior
error) and only clears it on `connected: true`. On a successful (re)connect the
sink clears `lastError` (runtime status patches merge, so a recovered transport
would otherwise keep surfacing the previous error). `running` is deliberately left owned by the monitor lifecycle and stays
`true` across transient reconnects — the same split the qqbot channel adopted in
#100127. This gives the shared health monitor (`evaluateChannelHealth`) the
`connected: false` signal it needs to notice and recover a dead Twitch transport.

The change deliberately does not publish `lastTransportActivityAt`: Twurple
exposes no heartbeat here, and the health monitor only runs its stale-socket
restart when `connected` is true *and* `lastTransportActivityAt` is set, so a
one-shot connect timestamp would age out and restart a quiet-but-healthy Twitch
account. Dead-transport recovery is driven by `connected: false` alone.

The other bundled channels (Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Feishu, Matrix,
WhatsApp, Telegram, and the webhook-based channels) already clear their
connection status on transport close, and the probe-based channels compute
liveness on demand — Twitch was the remaining channel that latched a live
status and never cleared it. The on-demand `probeTwitch` check is a separate,
independent throwaway-client credential test; it does not observe the live
monitor's chat client and the health monitor does not consult it, so the
persistent `connected` wiring is still required.

## User Impact

Operators running Twitch now see the account flip to disconnected in
`openclaw channels status` when its chat transport actually drops or a reconnect
fails authentication, instead of a permanently green status. This also lets the
channel health monitor detect and restart a dead Twitch transport automatically.
No configuration changes; the `running` field keeps its existing meaning.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior run.** A harness drives the real production code path —
`TwitchClientManager` (persistent readiness listeners), `monitorTwitchProvider`
(status sink), `twitchPlugin.status.buildChannelSummary`, and
`collectTwitchStatusIssues` — with only the external `@twurple/chat` transport
replaced by a controllable stub (no product code stubbed). The runtime status
store shallow patch-merges, matching the gateway status store. Output for
connect → drop → raw reconnect → auth failure → retry disconnect → auth success:

```
=== after initial connect ===
channels status -> {"running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null}
status issues -> (none)

=== after transport drop ===
channels status -> {"running":true,"connected":false,"lastError":"connection reset"}
status issues -> [ '[runtime] Last error: connection reset' ]

=== after raw reconnect (pre-auth) ===
channels status -> {"running":true,"connected":false,"lastError":"connection reset"}
status issues -> [ '[runtime] Last error: connection reset' ]

=== after reconnect auth failure ===
channels status -> {"running":true,"connected":false,"lastError":"Login authentication failed"}
status issues -> [ '[runtime] Last error: Login authentication failed' ]

=== after Twurple reasonless retry disconnect ===
channels status -> {"running":true,"connected":false,"lastError":"Login authentication failed"}
status issues -> [ '[runtime] Last error: Login authentication failed' ]

=== after reconnect auth success ===
channels status -> {"running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null}
status issues -> (none)
```

Before this change a raw socket reconnect flipped the status back to
`connected: true` before authentication settled, so an auth-failing reconnect
reported a false healthy status. The "reasonless retry disconnect" step models
Twurple's own `quit()`+`connect()` auth-retry, which fires a manual
reason-less `onDisconnect` immediately after the auth failure; the status sink
now preserves the auth-failure error across it instead of nulling it out.

**Note on proof scope.** The `@twurple/chat` transport is a controllable stub,
so this is not a redacted real-Twitch capture. Real connect → drop → auth-fail →
reconnect evidence from a live setup is still a pre-merge gap.

**Automated tests** (all Twitch extension tests pass):

- `extensions/twitch/src/twitch-client.test.ts` — the persistent listener drives
  `connected: true` from auth success (not raw `onConnect`); a raw transport
  connect owns no liveness listener, so it cannot report healthy pre-auth; a
  reconnect `onAuthenticationFailure` surfaces `connected: false` with the
  failure text; and a post-handshake `onDisconnect` notifies subscribers with
  `connected: false` and the disconnect reason.
- `extensions/twitch/src/monitor.status.test.ts` — the monitor forwards
  `onConnectionChange` to the status sink, and a disconnect-then-reconnect
  sequence clears the prior `lastError`.
- `extensions/twitch/src/plugin.lifecycle.test.ts` — driving the real
  `gateway.startAccount` path, a monitor-reported transport drop emits
  `connected: false` while `running` is never cleared; `buildChannelSummary`
  surfaces `connected`.

target.title: feat(android): hide thinking control and gate sends for models without reasoning support
target.body:
Related: #100699

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android chat users could set a thinking level for models that don't support configurable reasoning — the control silently did nothing, and worse, an explicit non-off level sent to such a model is rejected by the gateway (`agent-command.ts` throws for explicit unsupported levels), failing the send.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completes the reasoning-gating pack item on Android, mirroring the iOS behavior landed in #100875. A pure fail-open helper matches the selected model ref (from the in-chat picker landed in #100798) against the gateway model catalog's `supportsReasoning` flag: unknown/default selections keep the control (fail open); a matched non-reasoning model hides the thinking control (context meter shows a context-only label, composer dropdown hides the entries). The send boundary applies the same rule: gated sends carry `thinking: "off"` without mutating the stored level, so switching back to a reasoning-capable model restores the user's preference. Queued outbox sends re-evaluate the gate at flush for the active session only; unknown queued sessions deliberately fail open and keep their enqueue-time level (commented at the site) — identical to the iOS contract.

## User Impact

The thinking control on Android now appears only when it does something for the selected model, and sends can no longer fail because a stale thinking level hit a non-reasoning model.

## Evidence

- Focused Gradle suites green (30 tests + 5-test model-flip rerun): helper truth table (null/unknown/supported/unsupported), context-meter label with gating, gated send carries `off` while the stored level is preserved and restored on selection flip, outbox active-session gating and unknown-session fail-open.
- `corepack pnpm native:i18n:sync` run; snapshot consistent at head.
- ktlint: no findings on changed lines (full-project check red only on pre-existing violations in untouched files).
- Structured review (codex) — clean at head.

target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, prompt injection in those conversations can drive agent tool calls. The exposure matrix already flagged:

- elevated tools (`security.exposure.open_groups_with_elevated`)
- runtime/filesystem tools without sandbox or workspace guards (`security.exposure.open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs`)

It did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`) that can reconfigure the gateway or manipulate scheduled runs. A common example: `tools.profile="coding"` on an open WhatsApp group allows `cron` while runtime/fs may be sandboxed — the audit could report a clean runtime/fs posture while `cron` remained reachable from untrusted chat input.

### Gap 2: Extension plugin commands on chat command surfaces

The plugin trust audit warned when extensions existed without `plugins.allow`, but severity escalation depended only on **native skill commands** being enabled. It did not:

- evaluate **native command** surfaces separately from native skill commands
- name which configured channels expose command surfaces in the finding detail
- warn when **enabled extension plugins register commands** that may be reachable on those surfaces

Plugin commands bypass the LLM and run before built-in commands and agent invocation. Operators with Discord (or other channels) auto-enabling native commands and unallowlisted extensions could receive only a generic warn-level finding without understanding the bypass risk.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Control-plane exposure (sync audit)

`collectRiskyToolExposureContexts()` in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts` now probes `cron` and `gateway` alongside existing runtime/fs checks. Control-plane exposure is tracked in a separate `riskyControlPlaneContexts` list because sandbox mode does not mitigate gateway/cron control the way it mitigates exec/filesystem tools.

When open inbound policy is present and any agent context allows control-plane tools, the audit emits a new finding:

| Field         | Value                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkId`     | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane`                                                                                              |
| `severity`    | `critical`                                                                                                                                      |
| `remediation` | Deny `group:automation` (or explicitly deny `cron`/`gateway`) for exposed agents; keep control-plane tools limited to trusted operator sessions |

The multi-user heuristic (`security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic`) now includes control-plane context lines when present, and its impact summary distinguishes control-plane exposure from runtime/process exposure.

### Plugin command surface audit (async plugin trust)

`collectPluginsTrustFindings()` in `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts` adds `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()`, which resolves per-channel:

- **native commands** via `resolveNativeCommandsEnabled()` (respecting channel overrides, global `commands.native`, and plugin `nativeCommandsAutoEnabled`)
- **native skill commands** via `resolveNativeSkillsEnabled()` (existing behavior, now shared helper)

Changes to existing and new findings:

| `checkId`                                 | Before                                                       | After                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist`         | `warn`; critical only when native **skill** commands enabled | `critical` when **native commands or native skill commands** enabled on any configured channel; detail names affected surfaces |
| `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | _(did not exist)_                                            | `warn` when enabled extension plugins register commands **and** native commands are enabled on configured surfaces             |

The plugin registry snapshot is loaded once per audit pass and reused for phantom allowlist checks and command registration lookup. Command reachability is intentionally gated on **native commands** (not native skills alone) because plugin-registered commands route through the native command surface.

## User Impact

- **Operators** running `openclaw security audit` get clearer, actionable findings when open chats can reach gateway/cron control or extension plugin commands.
- **Severity changes**: `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` may now report `critical` on setups that previously showed `warn` when native commands (not just native skills) are active without `plugins.allow`.
- **No runtime behavior change**: gateway, tool policy, plugin loading, and command dispatch are unchanged. This is audit output only.

## Evidence

### Focused tests

```bash
pnpm test src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts
```

Result (local, macOS):

```text
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Duration  ~3s
```

### Trust-model test matrix (`audit-trust-model.test.ts`)

| Scenario                                                                     | Expected finding                                                                                                      | Severity |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Open WhatsApp group + `tools.profile="coding"`                               | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane`                                                                    | critical |
| Same + `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode="all"`                                  | No `open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs`; no `open_groups_with_control_plane` when automation denied by policy interaction | —        |
| Open group + `deny: ["group:automation"]`                                    | No `open_groups_with_control_plane`                                                                                   | —        |
| Discord allowlist + multi-user heuristic signals + runtime/automation denied | `security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic` detail includes `No exposed control-plane contexts detected.`             | warn     |

### Plugin trust test matrix (`audit-plugins-trust.test.ts`)

| Scenario                                                                            | Expected finding                                                                        | Severity |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Extensions present, no `plugins.allow`, no configured channels                      | `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist`                                                       | warn     |
| Extensions + configured Discord (native commands auto-enabled) + no `plugins.allow` | `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` with `Native commands are enabled` in detail          | critical |
| `plugins.allow=["some-plugin"]` + Discord + plugin registers commands               | `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` + `plugins.tools_reachable_permissive_policy` | warn     |
| Same + `tools.profile="coding"`                                                     | Command reachability warn; permissive tool policy **not** flagged                       | —        |
| Same + `commands.native=false`                                                      | No `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface`                                            | —        |
| Discord token via SecretRef env ref                                                 | Still critical `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` with bypass explanation                | critical |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Open ingress could reach control-plane tools and extension plugin commands without dedicated audit findings.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-audit-plugin-command-control-surface.mjs`
  2. `pnpm test src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-audit-plugin-command-control-surface.mjs
=== security audit: control-plane exposure (production collector) ===
[critical] security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane: Open group/DM policy with control-plane tools exposed
Found inbound policy="open" at:
- channels.whatsapp.groupPolicy
Risky control-plane contexts:
- agents.defaults (sandbox=off; control=[cron])
  ok: open group + coding profile emits security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane
  ok: plugin trust and trust-model regression tests pass
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Open WhatsApp group with `tools.profile="coding"` emits a critical control-plane finding naming `cron`; plugin trust and trust-model regression tests pass with command-surface coverage.
- **What was not tested:** Full `openclaw security audit --deep` against a live gateway; proof uses production collectors plus focused regression tests.

## Before / after behavior examples

### Example A: Open group with coding profile

**Config sketch:**

```json
{
  "channels": { "whatsapp": { "groupPolicy": "open" } },
  "tools": { "elevated": { "enabled": false }, "profile": "coding" }
}
```

**Before:** May flag runtime/fs exposure; `cron` allowed by coding profile not called out as control-plane risk.

**After:** Emits `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` naming contexts where `cron` (and `gateway` if allowed) are reachable.

### Example B: Discord + extensions, no allowlist

**Config sketch:**

```json
{
  "channels": { "discord": { "enabled": true, "token": "..." } }
}
```

(with extension directories present under state)

**Before:** `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` at `warn` unless native **skills** explicitly enabled.

**After:** `critical` because Discord native commands auto-enable on configured surfaces; detail lists `discord` and explains plugin commands bypass the LLM.

## Files changed

| File                                       | Change                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts`         | Control-plane probe; new exposure finding; multi-user heuristic detail                          |
| `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts`      | `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()`; severity/detail updates; new command reachability finding |
| `src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts`   | Control-plane and deny-path regression cases                                                    |
| `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts` | Native command surface mocks and command reachability cases                                     |

## Non-goals and boundaries

- Does not change tool allow/deny enforcement at runtime.
- Does not add new config keys or env vars.
- Does not scan plugin command handlers for code safety (existing `--deep` plugin code scan remains separate).

target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution already emits diagnostics when a configured SecretRef fails and provider env credentials are used instead (for example web-search/web-fetch fallback warnings and gateway token env fallback), but `openclaw security audit` and doctor did not surface that boundary drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a config-layer plugin load path collector that reuses existing discovery and doctor bundled-path helpers, then maps results to structured security audit findings (`plugins.load_paths.*`). Added a shared secrets diagnostic helper (`collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics`) used by both security audit (`secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`) and a new doctor health check (`core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`). This keeps runtime behavior unchanged while aligning audit/doctor output with existing runtime warnings.

## User Impact

- Operators running `openclaw security audit` now get early warnings when `plugins.load.paths` points at risky or missing locations, and when configured SecretRefs silently fall back to env credentials.
- `openclaw doctor` now emits structured warnings for SecretRef env fallback cases that previously only appeared in runtime/gateway logs.
- No config schema, runtime enforcement, or secret resolution behavior changes.

## Evidence

```bash
pnpm test src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts
pnpm test src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts
node --import tsx scripts/proof-audit-load-paths-secretref.mjs
```

- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0.
